summary: The bound portal validator accepted the regenerated current-release R-5 and R-10 artifacts with zero structural, teardown, broker/tenant, picker, safeguard, or redaction failures.

assertions.evidence: preConsentClosed, consentedOpenAndVisible, chatChangeClosed, hiddenPausedVisibleResumed, and disconnectClosed each carry event, predicate, structured result, and raw measured observations.

The validator proved pre-consent closure, consented capture visibility, chat-change teardown without late recapture, hidden false to visible true capture transitions, and disconnect closure with an explicit recovery control.
boundaryControl, brokerTenant, pickerNoFallback, and releaseSafeguards are all present and independently pass their required predicates.

A current-release source-runtime probe observed two hosted callers in one organization receiving distinct caller and route-budget scopes, two provider mints, and distinct short-lived conversations; another tenant remained admitted while the first caller was cooling down.
The deployed picker exposes the explicit unavailable ElevenLabs choice, reports elevenlabs=false and livekit=true, names the denial, and records zero LiveKit fallback calls.

Both public provider-start routes record a portal_voice_start_rate_limited 429 with Retry-After, and the artifact serializes no API key, auth secret, conversation token, provider token, or secret-bearing URL.
The bound readiness test rejects a false chat teardown, a missing brokerTenant group, and a serialized token field.
The current ten-file portal acceptance cohort passed 10 of 10 files and 223 of 223 tests after the validator and artifact regeneration; portal typecheck was clean.
